name: Milang
reason: Lakeside town with its own southaustralia.com destination page; heritage jetty, Port Milang railway museum (free, weekends) and historical walk give a half-day stop.

name: Wellington
reason: Searched southaustralia.com, themurrayriver.com, Wikivoyage: the only draw named is the free river ferry (transport, not a place); the old court house is now accommodation. No counted source names something to see or do.

name: Blanchetown
reason: For: southaustralia.com Riverland pages name Hunter Road Lookout over Lock 1 and the township, and the lock/old bridge with pelicans is a recommended photo stop. Against: the town itself has little more than a hotel and caravan park; the lookout is a short stop and likely its own candidate.

name: Kingston on Murray
reason: Small river township; southaustralia.com lists only a bridge lookout with a Sturt memorial (ten-minute stop, minor memorial) and a riverfront. No distinct half-hour draw. Moorook/Loch Luna game reserves are the nature draw.

name: Paringa
reason: Wikivoyage covers Paringa inside its Renmark article: a narrow 1927 bridge with a shared path and a small museum open three days a week 10-3. Too thin for its own spot; the town is part of Renmark's coverage.

name: Coonalpyn
reason: Coonalpyn Silos (Guido van Helten, 2017, South Australia's first silo art) are named on southaustralia.com as a free roadside attraction with picnic area; a quirky roadside icon travellers stop for.

name: Salt Creek
reason: A roadhouse settlement; Coorong NP page lists it as the start of the walking trails, which are separate candidates (Nukan Kungun Hike, Ngrugie Ngoppun, Lakes Nature Walk). Duplicate of those, nothing else to see.

name: Overland Corner
reason: National Trust's 1860 Overland Corner Hotel is also a heritage museum (artefacts, old post office) with walking trails in Overland Corner and Herons Bend reserves; a steward visitor page names it.

name: Cadell
reason: Wikivoyage mentions Cadell only as the proposed start of the Murray Coorong Trail (unbuilt); no source names anything to see at the township.

name: Cobdogla
reason: For: southaustralia.com names the Cobdogla Irrigation and Steam Museum (world-famous Humphrey pump, steam train ride, accredited railway). Against: volunteer-run with 'five major operating days each year' and the Humphrey Pump is under repair, so it is not reliably open when a visitor arrives. Name is the locality; the museum is the place.

name: Moorook
reason: Riverfront reserve and campground; the nature draw is Loch Luna and Moorook Game Reserves (a separate place, agency page lists only bushwalking and camping). Duplicate of that park.

name: Jack Point Pelican Observatory Walk
reason: Agency lists Jack Point as home of the largest Australian pelican breeding colony; 20-minute 1.2 km walk to a viewing area.

name: Parnka Point
reason: Agency attraction: Parnka Point ('Hells Gate') narrowest point between the lagoons, with views and birds; Parnka Ngoppun Trail 2-hour 5 km loop.

name: Long Point (Coorong)
reason: For: Coorong NP page lists Long Point under Attractions (jetty, sunset fishing over the lagoon). Against: essentially a campground and boat ramp with a jetty; little to see or do beyond fishing or camping.

name: Chinaman's Well Historic Site
reason: Agency attraction and 1-hour Journey to Gold Walk past the stone well, quarries and eating-house ruins.

name: Godfrey's Landing
reason: Agency attraction and Storm Boy filming location; boat-access walk through dunes to the ocean beach (1 hr, 3 km). Boat only, but a named place.

name: Lakes Nature Walk
reason: Agency easy walk: 3 km, 1 hour loop past ephemeral lakes and mallee.

name: Ngrugie Ngoppun Walk
reason: Agency easy walk: 2.5 km loop with wildlife viewing and local history.

name: Nukan Kungun Hike
reason: Agency two-day 25 km hike from Salt Creek to 42 Mile Crossing linking the park's walks; a multi-day walk a managing agency promotes.

name: 28 Mile Crossing
reason: Campground only; the agency's named crossing for beach access is 42 Mile Crossing (a different candidate). Nothing named to see at 28 Mile.

name: Ninety Mile Beach (Coorong)
reason: Agency names Ninety Mile Beach (4WD only) as a Storm Boy filming location on the Younghusband Peninsula ocean beach; Wikivoyage's Coorong Beach is the same stretch. If a separate Coorong ocean-beach candidate exists, treat as duplicate. Needs coordinates on the SA side.

name: Murray Mouth
reason: The visitor viewpoint Wikivoyage names (Murray Mouth Lookout, Sugars Ave) is on Hindmarsh Island, in sa-fleurieu per the region lines; the mouth is not a separate visitor point in this region.

name: Pink Lake (Meningie)
reason: Narrung and Lake Albert Scenic Loop Drive page (southaustralia.com) singles out the striking Pink Lake; pull-out with photo stop. Guide-named roadside natural feature, short visit.

name: Point Malcolm Lighthouse
reason: Australia's only inland lighthouse (1878), named by southaustralia.com and themurrayriver.com on the Narrung loop and cycle routes.

name: Raukkan Church
reason: 1868 church on the $50 note at Raukkan, named by southaustralia.com loop page and themurrayriver.com; landmark a guide singles out, with the Ngarrindjeri community welcoming visitors.

name: Lake Alexandrina
reason: Region-sized lake with no single visitor point; counted source only lists towns around it. The places to go are Milang, Point Malcolm and the Narrung loop.

name: Meningie Cheese Factory Museum
reason: Wikivoyage See listing and themurrayriver.com: volunteer-run local history museum in the old cheese factory, with restaurant.

name: Meningie Hill Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage See listing: 24/7 lookout over Meningie and Lake Albert; short stop but a guide names it.

name: Meningie Walking and Cycling Trails
reason: southaustralia.com lists Meningie Lions Walking Trail and the Meningie Walking and Cycling Trails (lookouts, lakeside); one place, merge the two listings.

name: Bushranger Birdman of the Coorong
reason: southaustralia.com free attraction: life-size saddled ostrich statue on the Meningie lake shore telling the Peggotty legend; quirky roadside icon (0-15 min).

name: Eagle View 4WD Track
reason: southaustralia.com: self-drive 4WD route through a private conservation and farming property, 32 km, $60 per car, booking required. Private land operator experience.

name: Spirit of the Coorong
reason: A cruise operator and vessel; the places it visits (the Coorong, Murray Mouth) are the spots.

name: Lower Murray Canoe Trail
reason: southaustralia.com free trail: about 21 km paddling route Tailem Bend to Wellington in four sections with interpretive signs; a promoted water trail. Marginal as no single point, so placement at Tailem Bend start.

name: Murray Coorong Trail
reason: Wikivoyage: a planned 250 km Cadell to Salt Creek trail, with only a 5 km Parnka Point section built (already Parnka Ngoppun Trail). Not an existing walkable route.

name: Sturt Reserve
reason: For: southaustralia.com lists it among Murray Bridge attractions: riverfront with cafe, barbecues, Bertha the Bunyip, playground. Against: an ordinary riverside town park, Bertha the Bunyip is its own listing, no distinct attraction.

name: Rocky Gully Wetlands
reason: Council tourism page and southaustralia.com: loop walk through wetlands with birdlife, picnic shelter, part of Lavender Federation Trail.

name: Swanport Wetlands
reason: southaustralia.com lists it (lookouts); nationally significant 19 ha River Murray wetland with interpretive trails and the Frank Jackman Memorial Lookout, wheelchair accessible.

name: Thiele Reserve
reason: southaustralia.com lists only a riverside reserve with barbecue and boat ramp; ordinary local reserve with no named sight.

name: The Round House (Murray Bridge)
reason: southaustralia.com and themurrayriver.com: heritage house museum, guided tours included in $8 entry, open several afternoons a week.

name: Lavender Federation Trail
reason: For: southaustralia.com has a journey page for the 325 km Murray Bridge to Clare walking trail, and it is a named long trail. Against: runs mostly through Adelaide Hills, Barossa and Clare regions, so its midpoint is outside this region; sections near Murray Bridge are already Rocky Gully Wetlands.

name: The Bend Motorsport Park
reason: A motorsport circuit sold as paid driver experiences, karting and ticketed race events (Wikipedia-high views come from events); no always-open sight for a visitor. Operator/venue for events.

name: Tailem Bend Historic Rail Trail
reason: southaustralia.com and themurrayriver.com: free marked heritage walk/drive with interpretive signs (railway cottages, institute); a guide's walking route. Short.
